name: Stability Ball Pike and Roll-In
description: A stability ball core and hip flexor exercise in which the exerciser begins in a push-up plank position with shins on the ball and then pikes the hips upward while rolling the ball in toward the hands. The pike position demands significant anterior core compression, hip flexor control, and shoulder stability simultaneously. The unstable ball surface amplifies the demand on all stabilizing muscles throughout the movement.

execution.starting_position: Begin in a push-up plank position with both shins resting on a stability ball and hands on the floor directly under the shoulders.
execution.setup_instructions: Use a fully inflated stability ball. Begin with the ball closer to the knees (less leverage) before advancing to the shins-on-ball position.
steps: Step 1: Begin in the plank with shins on the ball, body in a rigid straight line.
Step 2: Drive the hips upward toward the ceiling, rolling the ball in toward the hands. The body forms a pike (inverted V) at the top.
Step 3: Hold the pike position for 1-2 seconds.
Step 4: Slowly lower the hips and roll the ball back to the starting plank. Repeat.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as you pike the hips up. Inhale as you lower back to plank.
common_mistakes: Collapsing the lower back during the plank between repetitions
Rushing the rollout back to plank — control the return
Not achieving a true pike — hips must rise significantly above shoulder level for proper activation
safety_considerations: Requires shoulder stability and core strength — build both before attempting
If lower back pain occurs on the return to plank, brace the core more firmly or reduce range
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full pike with hips significantly above shoulder height. Full plank extension on the return.
execution.tempo_recommendations: 2s pike up, 2s hold, 3s slow rollout return.
coaching_cues: Drive the hips to the ceiling — think of an upside-down V
Keep the arms straight throughout — this is not a push-up
Slow on the way back down — control every inch of the rollout
